title: Rare and Intriguing Textiles Await Visitors in "Weaving an Empire: Textiles of the Inka World," through December 23
summary: A rare woman's dress that is 500 years old, a man's tunic depicting eight double-headed snakes, and one of the finest examples of an Inka elite tunic, featuring the classic "key" motif, are among the intriguing discoveries that await visitors to Weaving an Empire: Textiles of the Inka World , on view through December 23 at The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum in Washington, DC. The Textile Museum's first major exhibition of South American textiles in over 20 years reveals how Andean dress and other textiles in the 15th and 16th centuries reflected both the influence of the Inka and the diversity within their empire, which was one of the world’s largest and encompassed much of South America’s western region. title: Galerie Lelong announces the passing of legendary sculptor Ursula von Rydingsvard at 84
summary: Galerie Lelong announced the death of our beloved artist Ursula von Rydingsvard (b. 1942, Deensen, Germany – d. 2026, New York, New York). Ursula von Rydingsvard was an artist of inimitable strength with an enduring drive to create. At a time when few women artists were recognized as important sculptors, she worked beyond what seemed possible, expanding in scale and innovating her forms. For fifty years, she sculpted in her signature medium, cedar, sometimes translating the resulting sculptures to resin and bronze for outdoor installation. Using an intuitive approach, von Rydingsvard turned industrial four-by-four wooden beams into organic forms, using a circular saw and hand applying graphite patinas to form textured orifices that invigorate the utilitarian material with emotional charge. title: Muscarelle Museum of Art announces upcoming exhibition, "Judith Godwin: Bold Strokes"
summary: Trace the creative evolution of one of Abstract Expressionism’s most underrecognized artists with “Judith Godwin: Bold Strokes,” on view Feb. 12-May 30, 2027 at the Muscarelle Museum of Art at William & Mary. The retrospective spans nearly 50 years and features approximately 30 works that capture the dynamic interplay of gesture, form and motion central to Godwin’s work. “Judith Godwin was one of the most compelling voices in the Abstract Expressionist movement, but she painted during a time when women artists were often overlooked. ‘Bold Strokes’ examines the arc of her amazing and productive career, and celebrates her unbounded energy that resulted in a long sequence of powerful works,” said David Brashear, exhibition curator and director of the Muscarelle Museum of Art. title: Musée Matisse Nice pairs Henri Matisse and Alex Katz in landmark dialogue exhibition
summary: Every autumn, the Musée Matisse Nice explores contemporary perceptions of the work of Henri Matisse (1869–1954). This year, it is hosting a temporary exhibition dedicated to Alex Katz (born in 1927), a leading figure in American painting. The encounter between Henri Matisse and Alex Katz forms part of a vast cultural history linking France and the United States. Henri Matisse’s work was exhibited across the Atlantic from 1908 onwards and played a part in introducing the American public to the most avant-garde developments in European art. In February 1949, Alex Katz came across an exhibition at Pierre Matisse’s gallery in New York, which was dedicated to his father’s recent works. The paintings known as the “Intérieurs de Vence” (Interiors of Vence)—including Nature morte aux grenades (Still Life with Pomegranates) and Le silence habité des maisons (The Inhabited Silence of Houses)—along with the brush drawings and cut-outs, had a profound aesthe

title: Christie's brings more than USD$130 million of art to Abu Dhabi ahead of landmark auction
summary: Christie's announces more than USD$130 million worth of art in Abu Dhabi, bringing together highlights from its forthcoming New York 20/21 sales in November alongside MAWASIM: 20 Years of Modern and Contemporary Middle Eastern Art. A curated selection from Christie's Private Sales will also be on view at The Abu Dhabi EDITION ahead of the landmark MAWASIM auction on 1 November 2026, marking Christie's first fine art auction in Abu Dhabi. Three major works from Christie's upcoming New York 20/21 sales will be presented alongside the MAWASIM exhibition. Spanning abstraction and figurative painting, the selection reflects the breadth of artistic practice in 20th century Western art. title: Sotheby's Collectors' Week returns to Abu Dhabi
summary: This December, Sotheby's is set to stage a major week-long auction series in Abu Dhabi, spanning the realms of fine art and luxury. The second edition of Collectors' Week follows on from the historic inaugural series in December 2025. This year, the scope is even more ambitious, with the launch of Sotheby's first fine art auction in Abu Dhabi. Titled 'Breaking Ground', the sale is named in homage to the pioneering ethos of Abu Dhabi, where one of the most impressive cultural districts in the world has been forged from the ground up. The auction will offer works by the likes of Andy Warhol and Claude Monet, alongside leading figures of the Middle Eastern art world, with a spotlight on pioneering Emirati artists. The auctions will be preceded by public exhibitions, events, panel discussions and masterclasses that will welcome collectors from the UAE and around the world, and platform distinguished experts, cultural figures and dignitaries from across the region and beyond.

title: Fontana and Modigliani masterworks lead Christie's 20th/21st Century marquee week in Paris
summary: Christie's 20th/21st Century Art including - Evening Sale and the Art Contemporain - Vente du Jour attained exceptional results for the 2x25 works by Italian artists offered in this year's Thinking Italian sections, which marked the 25th anniversary of the sale concept. The group realized €28,106,640 with 92% works sold above their high estimates, driven by active participation from clients across 59 countries bidding in the room, by telephone and online. The top lot was Lucio Fontana's Concetto Spaziale, Mezzogiorno in Piazza S. Marco (1961), which achieved €6,815,000, closely followed by Amedeo Modigliani's Minoutcha (1916-17), which sold for €6,205,000 – representing the top 2 and 3 lots from the entire Paris 20/21 Marquee week. title: Dinosaur footprints dating back 65 million years discovered in Mexico
summary: A remarkable discovery in a quiet corner of western Mexico has opened a window onto a world that disappeared millions of years ago. What began with local residents noticing unusual markings in a streambed has turned into an important paleontological find: at least 50 fossilized dinosaur footprints, preserved in stone for approximately 65 million years. The tracks were discovered near San Juan de los Plátanos, a community in the municipality of Apatzingán, Michoacán. title: Harvard Art Museums welcome 2026 fellows
summary: The Harvard Art Museums announce the latest group of scholars in the museums’ longstanding Fellowship Program, designed to broaden the experience of those embarking on professional museum careers in art history and related fields, conservation and conservation science, and museum education. This group of eleven Fellows join the museums’ three curatorial divisions (Asian and Mediterranean Art, European and American Art, and Modern and Contemporary Art), the Division of Academic and Public Programs, and all four labs of the Straus Center for Conservation and Technical Studies (analytical, objects, paper, and paintings). During their one- or two-year appointments, participants in the Fellowship Program become integral members of staff, collaborating with colleagues across the institution. title: Harn Museum of Art opens year-long renovation project featuring a new art gallery and upgraded study center
summary: The Harn Museum of Art at the University of Florida opened its new 3,600 square-foot art gallery and 1,000 square-foot Bishop Study Center on Tuesday, Oct. 27. The renovation, which began in October 2025, allows visitors to see more art during their visit, with the first exhibition on view titled Beyond the Brush: The Florida Art Collection, Gift of Samuel H. and Roberta T. Vickers. The museum has remained open throughout the renovation, which also includes the named Drs. Rebecca & Paul Nagy Director’s Suite and Conference Room providing meeting space for staff and rental opportunities; upgrades to the Visitor Services area; and back-of-house catering walkway to assist in programs such as Art After Dark and the Harn’s event rental program. title: Sotheby's Paris achieves record-breaking $154.6M marquee auction week
summary: Bringing a remarkable week in Paris to a close, Sotheby's achieved its highest ever total for a series of marquee auctions in the city, with an overall total of €137.7m / $154.6m. Today's sales of Modernités and Surrealism & Its Legacy realised a combined total of €63.2m / $70.9m. The results follow yesterday's record-breaking auction of The Schlumberger Collection, which realised €74.4m / $83.7m. title: Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein presents major solo exhibition by Anna Jermolaewa
summary: With an empathetic eye and subtle humour, Anna Jermolaewa lays bare the hidden mechanisms of everyday life, her practice always very close to the reality of life. Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein is devoting a major solo exhibition to the Vienna-based artist (born in St Petersburg, 1970). Radical Hope combines selected earlier works with numerous new pieces created especially for the exhibition in Vaduz. For this purpose, Jermolaewa travelled to the Pyrenees to trace the path of Walter Benjamin and Lisa Fittko, who helped him escape Vichy France; then to Paris to meet with Aleksandra Wysokińska, who had helped the artist make her escape; and finally to the Channel Island of Jersey, where she shot material for the project in Gerald Durrell's sanctuary for endangered species. title: Mazzoleni closes 40th anniversary celebrations with Giorgio de Chirico exhibition
summary: The exhibition Giorgio de Chirico. The Contemporary Enigma ideally brings Mazzoleni's 40th anniversary celebrations to a close, presenting the work of Giorgio de Chirico, an artist who has been central to the family's collecting history and subsequently to the gallery's activity. The masterpieces of the pictor optimus are presented here in dialogue with a selection of works by established and contemporary artists who, in different ways, have drawn on his legacy, reinterpreting his style and most distinctive motifs across a period spanning from the 1930s to the present day. These open-ended juxtapositions suggest the idea of a "continuous Metaphysics": a visual language that runs throughout de Chirico's artistic trajectory and continues to resurface in the practices of subsequent generations. The contemporary enigma evoked by the title refers to the inexhaustible capacity of de Chirico's works to engage viewers and artists

title: Estorick Collection hosts intervention by Italian conceptual master Tino Stefanoni
summary: This autumn, the Estorick Collection presents a new intervention by the influential Italian painter and sculptor Tino Stefanoni (1937 – 2017), whose work bridges the gap between conceptual art, minimalism and Metaphysical painting. The works will be shown throughout the museum’s permanent collection from 28 October until 20 December 2026. One of the most original Italian artists of the 20th century, Stefanoni was inspired by Carlo Carrà, Giorgio Morandi, Giorgio de Chirico and Ottone Rosai, going on to develop a highly distinctive style that can be characterised as ‘conceptual figurative art’. The intervention at the Estorick Collection presents a selection of works from the artist’s key cycles as well as sculptures, multiples and special projects. title: The National Gallery launches an open call for a new digital experience
summary: Emerging UK-based creatives are invited to propose a playful and experimental digital experience to be displayed on the Gallery’s ‘Connected Canvas’ of high-definition screens in the Sainsbury Wing entrance. The National Gallery has today announced a new open call for an ambitious digital commission that makes use of its sophisticated visual and audio systems which were installed in the Sainsbury Wing Entrance as part of its refurbishment in 2025. The open call invites UK-based emerging creative practitioners, technologists, designers, multi-disciplinary teams and creative collectives to submit expressions of interest. Shortlisted applicants will be invited to a one-day workshop at the National Gallery before developing a final pitch. One project will be commissioned, for a total commission fee of £15,000. title: SMK Thy welcomes nearly 70,000 visitors in its first full season
summary: SMK Thy has just completed its first full season. A total of 68,038 people visited the new museum over the course of the year. On Sunday 18 October, SMK Thy welcomed its final visitors of the year before the museum in the small village of Doverodde closed at the end of its first full season. The season began on 28 March, and over the course of just under seven months, 68,038 people visited SMK Thy, which is part of SMK – National Gallery of Denmark. This brings the total number of visitors to 106,968 since the museum first opened its doors on 29 August 2025. This year, visitors could enjoy the critically acclaimed exhibition Living Landscapes, which drew on SMK’s extensive art collection to explore the relationship between humanity and nature. title: New Taipei City Art Museum presents Lim Kac-keong: Cosmos in View
summary: The development of Taiwanese art in the early twentieth century was shaped by shifts in the global political landscape and grew increasingly diverse through movements across geographic, cultural, and historical boundaries. Lim Kac-keong (1901–1992) was born into the Lin Ben Yuan family of Banqiao, Taiwan. In his youth, he lived at Shuzhuang Garden on the southeastern tip of Kulangsu Island in Xiamen. He later traveled to Britain, France, and Switzerland, undertaking twelve years of formal academic training in art. From 1938 to 1949, amid the upheavals of the period, he and his family moved repeatedly between Xiamen, Hong Kong, and Australia. title: Maruani Mercier now representing the Estate of Georg Karl Pfahler
summary: Maruani Mercier announced its representation of the Estate of Georg Karl Pfahler. Born in Emetzheim, Germany, in 1926, Pfahler was a pioneering figure of European Hard-Edge painting and postwar abstraction. After studying in Nuremberg, he continued his education at the Kunstakademie Stuttgart under Willi Baumeister, graduating in 1954. Initially influenced by Art Informel, he began to simplify his forms in the late 1950s, developing the Formativ series and the distinctive visual language for which he became known: bold geometric compositions, sharply defined forms, and vibrant, contrasting fields of color. For Pfahler, color was more than a formal element; it could shape perception and transform the experience of space. title: Saint-Gaudens's 'Victory' brings a monumental American story to Heritage Auctions Nov. 13
summary: She strides ahead of General William Tecumseh Sherman at the southeastern entrance to Central Park, a winged figure whose movement helped inspire the Liberty that would grace America’s most celebrated gold coin. Behind that enduring image stands another story: Hettie Anderson, the Black model whose poise and physical discipline helped Augustus Saint-Gaudens give a national ideal human form. On Nov. 13, Heritage Auctions will offer a rare gilded bronze reduction of Saint-Gaudens’s Victory as the centerpiece of its American Art Signature® Auction. title: Heritage's Nov. 18 Silver Auction showcases the masters of British and American silversmithing
summary: In the hands of an expert silversmith, even the most practical household implement can become an object of remarkable craftsmanship and beauty. That marriage of artistry and utility lies at the heart of Heritage Auctions' Nov. 18 Fine Silver & Objects of Vertu Signature® Auction, which brings together exceptional examples of English and American silver alongside distinctive works from Europe and Asia. With particular strength in British silver of the 18th and 19th centuries and American silver of the 19th century, the auction offers collectors an opportunity to explore the history of silversmithing through celebrated makers, ingenious forms and objects created to bring elegance and ceremony to everyday life. title: Indian rarities, 1921 Canadian 5 cents leads global treasures in Heritage's World & Ancient Coins Auction
summary: A remarkable lineup of Indian rarities will take center stage in Heritage's Nov. 5-6 World & Ancient Coins Platinum Session and Signature® Auction, offering collectors an exceptional opportunity to pursue some of the most coveted treasures in Indian numismatics. The selection anchors an auction of approximately 400 lots, with additional highlights from Great Britain, Canada, Mexico, Russia and beyond. "This is a succinct, well-curated auction, with an impressive variety of scarce types that will appeal to collectors at every level," says Kyle Johnson, Heritage's Managing Director of World & Ancient Coins. title: 'Beyond Visible Reality' and Walter Grab survey open parallel shows at Galerie Peter Kilchmann
summary: Galerie Peter Kilchmann presents Beyond Visible Reality, a group exhibition bringing together thirteen artistic positions that explore the space between dream and reality, abstraction and figuration. Contemporary painting today occupies a fascinating field of tension. While the photographic reproduction of reality has long since been taken over by digital media, many artists are searching for other forms of experiencing and depicting the world. Their paintings depict people, landscapes, and objects that remain recognisable, yet elude an objective representation of reality. They are neither classical Surrealist works nor realistic depictions of the world. Rather, these works inhabit an in-between space in which memory, dreams, imagination, personal experience, and psychological states merge into new pictorial realities. Reality is not reproduced,

title: Jessica Silverman unveils GaHee Park's major solo exhibition, 'Soft Shell'
summary: Jessica Silverman announced GaHee Park’s first solo show in the gallery’s large space, running October 28–December 19, 2026. Raised in Seoul, South Korea, Park completed degrees in Philadelphia and New York before moving to her current home base in Montreal, Canada. Her neo-surrealist paintings complicate the boundaries between interior and exterior, fantasy and reality, viewer and viewed. Featuring 13 new oil paintings, the exhibition showcases her signature figures and still lifes that often mutate into landscapes. The exhibition takes its title, “Soft Shell,” from what Park describes as “the containers of life that we inhabit to feel safe, but which do not protect us completely.” Throughout the show, protection takes many physical forms, such as conches, fruit skins, fingernails, and fish scales.
